subject.title: [Feature]: Add Support for System/Custom HTTP & SOCKS Proxy Configuration in OpenClaw

question: Should OpenClaw expand the current HTTP(S)-only managed proxy design to support SOCKS and per-surface proxy overrides, or keep the current explicit managed HTTP(S) proxy plus narrow owner-specific settings?
rationale: The remaining asks define new config/default behavior, proxy precedence, browser egress, bypass behavior, and credential handling across security-sensitive runtime surfaces, which repository policy treats as maintainer product/security direction rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design a broader proxy contract
options.body: Define a maintainer-approved proxy precedence model covering managed HTTP(S), SOCKS, env fallback, NO_PROXY, browser/profile routing, and per-surface overrides before implementation.

options.title: Keep current managed proxy scope
options.body: Leave SOCKS and per-surface overrides to owner-specific plugin, channel, or browser settings if maintainers decide broader core proxying is out of scope.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Move implementation to specific items such as web_fetch env detection, browser-profile proxying, and channel-owned proxy gaps while keeping this issue as umbrella context.

recommendation.title: Design a broader proxy contract
recommendation.body: Define a maintainer-approved proxy precedence model covering managed HTTP(S), SOCKS, env fallback, NO_PROXY, browser/profile routing, and per-surface overrides before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the central managed proxy feature that the remaining product direction would expand or deliberately constrain.
